主要内容: A U.S. federal judge approved a plan to restructure $17 billion of debt from Puerto Rico's Sales Tax Financing Corporation, COFINA. This marks the second deal between the bankrupt U.S. commonwealth and its creditors to win court approval. The plan will slash debt service on the sales tax-backed debt by $17.5 billion over nearly 40 years, saving the island an average $456 million annually. Future sales tax revenue previously pledged exclusively to COFINA will be split, with 53 percent going to COFINA bondholders and 46 percent flowing to the commonwealth government. Opposition came mainly from labor unions, which alleged the plan would drive away resources from essential public services. Owners of more than $14.5 billion of COFINA bonds voted in support of the plan. The judge acknowledged objections, including the lack of a comprehensive debt audit, and noted that the island's core government debt, including $13 billion of general obligation bonds and $50 billion in unfunded pension liabilities, must still be addressed.

股票实体.名称: Puerto Rico's Sales Tax Financing Corporation
